summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits Dell Technologies ahead of its earnings report and investor update, asking whether it is a buying opportunity again after a wild round trip. Dell was one of his better picks for years, but he downgraded it earlier this year when the price rose above $400; the stock then soared to $600 before crashing back to around $350, and it now trades at $377 after a 13% single-day jump. Wall Street analysts expect roughly 38% earnings-per-share growth each year for the next few years on booming AI data-centre server demand, while the consumer segment struggles as surging component prices dampen PC and laptop demand, a headwind expected into at least mid-next year. Dell's operating margin is at a record high of 9.9%, return on invested capital is also at a record high, and its made-to-order model keeps inventory costs low, though rivals Super Micro and Hewlett Packard Enterprise operate on similarly thin margins. Valuation has compressed to a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 12.44, down from about 19 earlier this year but still above the four to five times level of early 2026. His discounted cash flow fair value is $287 per share versus the $377 price, so the stock looks overvalued on that basis and fairly valued on earnings. Call: DELL HOLD at $377, fair value $287, first tracked, reiterating the hold he set earlier this year and repeated on 17 August — not a buy at these levels, especially with earnings volatility ahead.
title: Should You Buy Dell Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
